proposals.subtype: Define a mutable public administrator-contact model
proposals.explanation: AdministratorContact exposes four settable string properties for email, first name, last name and phone. These declarations define the public data shape without local validation; its empty parameterless constructor is not separately counted.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This complete source is directly under src, outside Generated, and is handwritten under the supplied .NET rule; the property surface is substantive rather than an empty partial stub.

proposals.subtype: Map administrator JSON field names into public properties
proposals.explanation: ReadProperties enumerates object properties, maps first_name/last_name/email/phone through GetString and ignores unrecognized names. It supplies no local schema validation or default switch action.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src model explicitly implements this JSON property switch rather than delegating to a generated serializer.

proposals.subtype: Omit null or empty administrator contact fields from JSON
proposals.explanation: WriteProperties writes each of the four contact strings only when it is neither null nor empty, using the cached encoded JSON names. It writes properties into an existing writer, not a complete enclosing JSON object.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src model contains the explicit per-field guards and Utf8JsonWriter calls.

proposals.subtype: Read certificate attributes with Unix-second timestamp conversion
proposals.explanation: CertificateAttributes.ReadProperties switches over seven JSON names, reads enabled/retention/recovery values, and converts nbf, exp, created and updated Int64 values through DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds. Unrecognized fields are ignored; the supplied struct contains no writer.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The internal struct and executable reader reside under src outside Generated, covered by the supplied .NET handwritten-source rule.

proposals.subtype: Adapt backup bytes to a base64url JSON value
proposals.explanation: CertificateBackup's explicit JSON reader decodes a present value property with Base64Url.Decode; its writer encodes Value into that property with Base64Url.Encode. The shared codec implementations and null/error behavior are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src class explicitly implements IJsonDeserializable and IJsonSerializable around its byte-array value.

proposals.subtype: Wire challenge authentication into an owned shared pipeline
proposals.explanation: The constructor validates URI/credential, defaults options, creates ChallengeBasedAuthenticationPolicy with the public verification-disable flag and installs it per retry in a newly owned pipeline. It passes that pipeline and diagnostics to both the internal certificates client and legacy KeyVaultPipeline wrapper. The imported policy implementation and the version-mapping helper are not captured.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client explicitly builds the pipeline and composes the internal client; the supplied .NET rule identifies this source as handwritten, not merely a dependency reference.

proposals.subtype: Expose the configured vault URI on the public client
proposals.explanation: The public virtual VaultUri getter returns the constructor-assigned _vaultUri field. It exposes configuration, not a remote lookup or a URI validation routine.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The public property is implemented on the handwritten src client rather than simply re-exporting the internal generated client.

proposals.subtype: Release an owned pipeline through an atomic null exchange
proposals.explanation: Dispose exchanges _ownedPipeline with null, disposes the returned value when present and suppresses finalization. This body does not show the pipeline's internal disposal rules or protect active operations from concurrent disposal.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src wrapper implements IDisposable and this executable ownership-lifecycle method.

proposals.subtype: Adapt generated create responses into a public certificate operation
proposals.explanation: The sync/async start-create methods validate inputs, start a named diagnostic scope with certificate-name metadata, serialize a request model, call the internal CreateCertificate operation, deserialize operation properties and construct CertificateOperation with this client. Older hidden overloads forward a null preserve-order option. Exceptions caught inside the try mark the scope failed; no custom polling algorithm or wire-compatibility result is demonstrated.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The src wrapper outside Generated contains the complete start-method bodies around an explicit internal generated-client call and public operation construction.

proposals.subtype: Forward a flattened download overload through an options object
proposals.explanation: The public EditorBrowsable(Never) DownloadCertificate overload constructs DownloadCertificateOptions from the name, assigns Version and forwards the cancellation token. Its target overload is not supplied, so certificate downloading, secret access and format conversion are not attributed to this body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src client contains this explicit executable overload adapter; it is not an inference from the download documentation.

proposals.subtype: Register client factories from a vault URI or configuration
proposals.explanation: The two AddCertificateClient extensions register either a URI/credential/options constructor factory or a configuration-based factory. The configuration overload declares trimming/dynamic-code warning attributes; binding implementation and runtime factory behavior are outside the supplied source.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These executable extension methods are defined in a non-generated src file under Microsoft.Extensions.Azure, covered by the .NET source rule.

proposals.subtype: Enumerate service versions and map them to wire version strings
proposals.explanation: CertificateClientOptions exposes nine service-version choices and a get-only Version, defaults its constructor to the preview LatestVersion and maps recognized values to wire strings. proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src options class explicitly defines the enum, constructor/default and switch mapping rather than referencing a dependency's version list.

proposals.subtype: Define a mutable public certificate-management contact model
proposals.explanation: CertificateContact exposes settable Email, Name and Phone strings. Its empty constructor is not independently counted; JSON reading and writing are separate implemented behaviors.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete model source is outside Generated under src, where the supplied .NET rule classifies handwritten model/API definitions.

proposals.subtype: Read contact properties through an explicit JSON-name switch
proposals.explanation: The explicit IJsonDeserializable reader enumerates the object, reads name/email/phone with GetString and ignores unknown names. No additional validation or custom error recovery is implemented in this method.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated src model implements this reader directly through the shared JSON interface.

proposals.subtype: Omit null or empty certificate-contact strings from JSON
proposals.explanation: The explicit writer emits name, email and phone only when nonempty, using cached encoded property names. It supplies properties to a surrounding JSON object rather than starting or ending that object.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src model contains each serialization guard and writer call.

proposals.subtype: Expose an extensible certificate-content-type string value
proposals.explanation: The readonly CertificateContentType struct rejects null constructor input, exposes two known MIME values, supports implicit string construction, compares backing values ordinally, and implements hash/display forwarding. It represents content-type names, not certificate-format conversion; the complete value-type contract is grouped as one instance.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete non-generated src file explicitly implements this public typed-string value and its operators rather than merely re-exporting a generated type.

decisions.reason: AdministratorContact.cs:11-38 declares a nonempty public model with four mutable properties directly under src, outside Generated. This is one public model-shape instance under the supplied .NET rule; the empty constructor adds no separate behavior.

AdministratorContact.ReadProperties at lines 40-65 explicitly switches on four wire names and assigns strings. The cited non-Generated source supports this distinct read-side serialization behavior, not a claim about error handling.

AdministratorContact.WriteProperties at lines 67-93 tests each field with string.IsNullOrEmpty before writing an encoded-name JSON property. It does not create the enclosing object; the proposal accurately describes the observed write-side behavior.

CertificateAttributes.ReadProperties at lines 33-68 maps the seven named JSON fields and converts four timestamp integers using DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds. The non-Generated src location and concrete method body support this reader as one instance.

CertificateBackup.cs:16-27 implements both JSON interfaces explicitly, decoding value with Base64Url.Decode and encoding Value with Base64Url.Encode. Codec internals and runtime failure handling are not in the evidence; the finding does not attribute those behaviors.

CertificateClient.cs:91-122 instantiates ChallengeBasedAuthenticationPolicy with the option at CertificateClientOptions.cs:97-100, installs it per retry in a built pipeline, and shares that pipeline with both clients. This establishes handwritten auth wiring, not a newly implemented policy or proof of the comments' wire-compatibility assertions.

CertificateClient.cs:98 and 124-127 show _vaultUri assigned by the constructor and exposed by the public virtual VaultUri property. This is a discrete public client-surface behavior, not an endpoint discovery or validation claim.

CertificateClient.Dispose at lines 136-140 atomically exchanges and disposes the owned pipeline, then suppresses finalization. The actual body supports ownership cleanup, without establishing concurrent-operation safety or the transport's internal disposal rules.

CertificateClient.cs:183-204 and 245-266 show handwritten adaptation of a generated create response to CertificateOperation, but no custom polling algorithm or poller implementation. The proposed lro-custom-poller pattern implies unsupported behavior; name the reusable public-operation adaptation instead.

finding.subtype: Wrap generated create responses in a public certificate operation
finding.explanation: The synchronous and asynchronous StartCreateCertificate bodies validate inputs, add certificate-name diagnostics, serialize CertificateCreateParameters, call _generated.CreateCertificate or CreateCertificateAsync, deserialize operation properties and return a CertificateOperation bound to this client. The older hidden overloads forward to these bodies with preserveCertificateOrder set to null. The captured code does not implement a polling algorithm.
finding.handwrittenRationale: These executable wrapper bodies reside in CertificateClient.cs directly under src, outside Generated, and explicitly compose a generated-client call with a public operation and handwritten mapping; whether a generator could replace the mapping depends on uncaptured context.

decisions.reason: CertificateClient.DownloadCertificate at lines 301-304 is a concrete public overload forwarding a constructed options object and token. It is a convenience adapter; the uncaptured target method's download or conversion behavior is not part of this finding.

CertificateClientBuilderExtensions.cs:19-34 defines two AddCertificateClient registration overloads with constructor and configuration-based factories. The trimming and dynamic-code attributes are visible, but the registered factories' execution and configuration binder internals are not.

CertificateClientOptions.cs:19-80 enumerates nine API versions and the Version property; lines 90-116 select a preview default and map known values to wire strings, throwing for unmatched values in GetVersionString. The constructor does not itself validate the version, as the proposal correctly distinguishes.

CertificateContact.cs:28-41 exposes three mutable public contact properties in a non-Generated src model. This public data shape is separate from its explicit JSON reader and writer; its empty constructor is not counted separately.

CertificateContact.cs:43-62 explicitly reads name, email and phone by a JSON-name switch, with field constants at lines 13-15. The code supports read-side mapping and does not demonstrate an error recovery policy.

CertificateContact.cs:64-80 guards each string with string.IsNullOrEmpty before writing it under the encoded JSON name defined at lines 17-19. This supports the separate conditional write behavior, not a complete enclosing JSON serializer.

CertificateContentType.cs:12-33 and 41-69 implement a public extensible string-valued struct with constructor null check, known MIME values, conversion, equality, hash and display methods. The source does not perform certificate-format conversion; grouping the value type's contract as one instance is appropriate.
